title: @object-ui/mobile: shell mode — detect `window.ObjectStackNative` and adapt the Console when the mobile shell hosts it
body:
## Context

`objectstack-ai/mobile` 2.0 is now a native shell around the web Console (objectstack-ai/mobile#144). It loads `https://<server>/_console/` in a WebView and injects a bridge, `window.ObjectStackNative`, before the Console's own scripts run. Today the Console does not know it is hosted, so it shows desktop chrome inside a phone frame. The shell also pads the WebView with the safe area itself and lifts its loading cover only on the WebView's load event.

The bridge contract is in `docs/HYBRID-SHELL.md` of the mobile repository (section "Native bridge"):

- `ObjectStackNative.version`, `platform`, `appVersion`, `capabilities`, `has(capability)`;
- `safeArea`, also published as CSS variables `--os-native-safe-top|bottom|left|right`;
- events `ready()` and `routeChanged(route)`;
- calls `getPushToken()`, `haptic(kind)`, `openExternal(url)`, `navigate(route)`, `resetServer()`, each returning a Promise.

## Ask

In `ui/packages/mobile` (`@object-ui/mobile`):

1. Add a `useNativeHost()` hook. It returns the bridge when `window.ObjectStackNative` is present, otherwise `null`. Check lazily at use time, not once at module load: on older Android WebViews the injection can land after the first page scripts.
2. In shell mode the Console:
   - hides the desktop-only chrome;
   - pads with the `--os-native-safe-*` variables;
   - calls `ready()` once the first screen is interactive;
   - calls `routeChanged(route)` on every SPA navigation.
3. Typed wrappers for the bridge calls, so Console features feature-detect with `has('haptic')` and never call a missing method.

## Acceptance

- With a fake `window.ObjectStackNative` installed before boot, the Console renders shell mode and `ready` is posted once.
- Without the global, the Console behaves as today.
- Unit tests cover detection, late injection, and the `ready` / `routeChanged` posts.

Governing text: ADR-0026 is not involved (no third-party UI code). The bridge contract lives in the mobile repository, `docs/HYBRID-SHELL.md`.
